en.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Proves Video Games Are the MCU's Next Storyboard
en.summary: Forget the comics. **Spider-Man: Brand New Day**'s monumental box office success reveals a new blueprint for Hollywood blockbusters. Video games might just be the ultimate source material.
en.body:
Marvel has a long and sometimes rocky history with adapting its comic book lore. Fans have often lamented departures from source material, from the truncated portrayal of **Gorr the God Butcher** in *Thor: Love and Thunder* to the controversial introduction of **Star-Lord**'s parentage in *Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2*. However, with the integration of former Fox properties and the introduction of characters like **Jean Grey**, the MCU's roster is expanding. But what if the studio's strongest blueprint wasn't found on the printed page at all?

**Spider-Man: Brand New Day** has shattered expectations, crossing the $2 billion mark globally and becoming the highest-grossing film of the year, even outperforming *Avengers: Endgame*'s domestic debut. This colossal success for the latest **Spider-Man** installment, directed by **Destin Daniel Cretton**, highlights a powerful trend: using video games not just as inspiration, but as effective storyboards for action-packed cinema. Cretton, known for his visually dynamic fight choreography in *Shang-Chi*, has delivered a film that blends spectacle with grounded character work, a feat that owes a debt to the intricate design and narrative arcs found in modern gaming.

## A New Direction for Blockbusters

The film's reception is a testament to the power of interactive entertainment as a narrative foundation. **Tom Holland**, who reprises his role as **Peter Parker**, has openly discussed his personal passion for gaming, even playing *Uncharted* while filming *Spider-Man: Homecoming* before starring as **Nathan Drake** in its film adaptation. This personal connection likely informed the approach to **Brand New Day**, which masterfully translates the visual language and pacing of acclaimed games like Insomniac's 2018 **Marvel's Spider-Man** into a cinematic experience. The result is an action movie that feels both familiar to gamers and accessible to newcomers, proving that a well-crafted game can offer a more potent and ready-made blueprint than decades of comic history.

## What the Fans Are Saying

The overwhelming positive response to **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** suggests a community eager for this kind of adaptation. Critics and audiences alike have praised its blend of "grounded characters and well-timed emotional beats" alongside its "dance-like battles" and "iconic frames." The film’s success, earning an impressive 8.0/10 rating on IMDb, indicates that this approach resonates deeply. It’s a movie that delivers on "big-screen spectacles, popcorn, and escapism" while retaining a core of relatable humanity, a delicate balance many superhero films struggle to achieve. This success story is a clear signal that audiences are ready for more ambitious adaptations that leverage the strengths of other media.

## What's Next

With **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** setting a new standard, all eyes are on future Marvel projects and how they might incorporate lessons learned from this blockbuster. The film's release date was July 31, 2026, and its unprecedented success guarantees that this game-inspired approach will be a major focus for studios looking to replicate its magic.

content_raw: Marvel sucks at following its comic source material. Even if that’s not always a problem, it is a commonly acknowledged fact amongst the fandom who have mourned the design and quick dispatching of Gorr the God Butcher in Thor: Love and Thunder or the introduction of Star-Lord as Ego’s son storyline in Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 . Marvel’s acquisition of 21st Century Fox has now allowed for the MCU to include many key figures that were missing from some of the most important story adaptations that it took from the comics. The introduction of Sadie Sink’s Jean Grey, along with the origins of the mutant inhibitors, shows that Marvel is now on a new trajectory that includes a full roster of fan-favorite characters. But what if the studio didn’t need to follow comic sources at all? What if there’s another medium that can provide a stronger blueprint? Spider-Man: Brand New Day has broken the $2 billion mark at the box office — making it the highest-grossing film of this year and the 4th highest-grossing movie of all time . It has been arguably the biggest success that the MCU has seen yet, outperforming Avengers: Endgame’s $357 million box-office domestic debut with $360 million. The MCU and Sony’s fourth Spidey joint venture succeeded in something that Hollywood has been trying to do with varying results – using games as effective source material, or more accurately: the storyboard. Mr. Spider-Man himself, Tom Holland, has been an active gamer for years, having spoken to ScreenRant in 2022 about playing Uncharted while filming Spider-Man: Homecoming . Holland would go on to play Nathan Drake, Uncharted ’s main protagonist in the film adaptation. He has also been vocal about using Insomniac Games’ 2018 video game Marvel’s Spider-Man , available on Steam and PlayStation, as inspiration for the action scenes of the newest web-slinger’s film. “For me, a lot of those finishing moves, a lot of our stuff was influenced by that stuff,” he told IGN . However, it wasn’t just him who was inspired by the games during the filming process — Holland explained in further detail how the action designers are also gamers. “A lot of the action designers and stunt people we had were huge gamers,” he explained. “They were able to experience things in those games that made them excited, and they would just screengrab the moves they really liked and bring them into the writers’ room and show it to me. And then we’d be like, ‘Yeah, that’s sick. Let’s try to figure out how to do that for real.’”  While the film took elements from the game, it didn’t use it as a bible for the storyline. Trying to use any other iteration of a Peter Parker adaptation would have backfired. One, because Holland’s Peter was erased from the memories of everyone he’s encountered, and two, because his Peter had strayed far from the street-level supe initially depicted by Tobey Maguire, Andrew Garfield, and Marvel’s Spider-Man actor Yuri Lowenthal.
